cohort: Neonates diagnosed with transient tachypnea of the newborn (TTN) at E-Da Hospital, excluding those with congenital anomalies, unstable vital signs, or maternal infections.
finding: The second C-reactive protein (CRP) measurement, taken 12-24 hours after birth, was identified as the only independent predictor of bacteremia in neonates with TTN, suggesting that delaying the initial blood test can effectively predict bacteremia.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery had minimal predictive value for neonatal bacteremia.
